Change order status via API from SUBMITT: The report's own description for this scenario ("verify it succeeds") is OUTDATED. Fixed via an explicit ALLOWED_STATUS_TRANSITIONS map in OrdersService.updateStatus() (commit "fix(orders): reject SUBMITTED -> DRAFT status rollback (409)"). Correct behavior: PATCH /orders/{id}/status changing SUBMITTED -> DRAFT MUST return 409 Conflict, message matching "Cannot transition order {id} from SUBMITTED to DRAFT". Write this as an edge_case asserting the 409 and the message — NOT success.
Attempt to edit SUBMITTED order: The report is ambiguous ("may be allowed or blocked"). It is not ambiguous in reality: OrdersService.updateItems() rejects any order where status !== 'DRAFT' with the same 409 Conflict pattern as delete. Write this as an edge_case asserting 409.
Verify Kafka event on order submission: PATCH /orders/{id}/status returns a JSON ARRAY of two objects, [updatedOrder, newOrderStatusHistoryEntry] — NOT a single order object. Do not assert a body_field against its top-level response (there is no top-level "status" field on an array). To confirm the status actually changed, use a db_row assertion against the Order table (where id={orders.id}, expectedFields.status), and/or rely on the kafka_message assertion alone.
Delete customer with existing orders: The report's own description ("verify behavior — cascading delete or error") is ambiguous. It is not ambiguous in reality: CustomersService.remove() checks the customer's order count first and throws a ConflictException (409) with message "Cannot delete customer {id}: they have {orderCount} order(s)" whenever it is greater than zero — no cascading delete happens. Write this as an edge_case asserting a 409 status and an error_message matching that pattern (not a successful deletion).
